paragraphs: The iPhone 18e’s camera bump could be hard to miss. Apple’s affordable phone might swap its flush lens for a raised, squarish camera plateau.
The iPhone 17e has no real bump at all, just a lens set into the glass. But according to a leaked redesign, Apple’s pocket-friendly phone could look a lot more like the Pro models.

Early iPhones featured relatively small camera humps, with lenses that barely protruded from the back of the devices. But as Apple added larger sensors, more sophisticated optics, and additional lens, the camera bumps grew increasingly prominent. On Pro models, they eventually became substantial raised platforms housing multiple lenses.

The iPhone 17e was something of a throwback, with a single rear camera sitting almost flush with the back glass. That gave it a cleaner, simpler look reminiscent of earlier iPhones. But its successor could usher in a change.

A report by Engadget’s Filipe Esposito, who claims to have seen CAD images of the iPhone 18e, says it has an almost square camer bump measuring 28 mm by 35 mm. That reportedly houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the microphone.
The images reportedly come from a source within Apple’s supply chain. Engadget says the source previously shared accurate tips on the iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro colors.

As per the leak, the plateau could look similar to the camera module on the M5 iPad Pro or the bump on earlier iPhone Pros. (The iPhone 17 Pro’s aluminum unibody redesign added a wider camera plateau that stretches almost the full width of the phone.)
The same files reportedly include CAD images of the base iPhone 18 and the iPhone Air 2 as well. Neither of those devices appears to get the new plateau.
